get.description:
Return the decks the player can choose from to start a match.

The AI plays another one of them.

post.description:
Start a match against the AI, which plays another faction's own deck.

The player plays a faction's own deck (``deck``) or, while logged in, one
they built (``my_deck``): the match keeps a copy of it, so changing or
deleting the deck later doesn't change the match (ADR 0017).

``level`` is how well the AI plays, ``easy`` when the request doesn't say
(ADR 0018). If the AI starts, it plays until it is the player's turn, and
its moves come with the match. The ``Location`` header of the response
holds the address of the match. If the player is logged in, the match is
theirs.

get.description:
Return the matches of the player who is logged in, newest first.

A page holds up to 20. For the next one, ``before`` is the id of the last
match of this one. If the player isn't logged in, the answer is a 401.
Return a match as the player may see it.

post.description:
Play the player's action, and then let the AI answer, at the match's level.

The action is one of the legal actions in the player's view, sent back as
it is, with the version of the match that came with that view. If the
match is at another version, the answer is a 409 and the match doesn't
change: get it again to see where it is. That is so also when another
request for the same match is played first, while this one is. If the
action isn't legal now, the answer is a 409 too.

If the match ends, the store keeps how it ended with the last actions.

get.description:
Return how the player's matches ended with each deck they played.

If the player isn't logged in, the answer is a 401.

Return what a player may put in a deck they build from a faction's cards.

``deck_id`` is the id of the faction's own deck, from ``GET /decks``.

Return the decks of the player who is logged in, the oldest first.

If the player isn't logged in, the answer is a 401.

post.description:
Build a deck and keep it for the player who is logged in.

The deck must keep to the rules (``GET /decks/{id}/choices``), and a
player may keep up to 10 decks (409 when they have 10).

put.description:
Change a deck of the player's: its name, faction and copies, all at once.

As when it was built, the deck must keep to the rules.

delete.description: Delete a deck of the player's.

post.description:
Make an account, and log in with it.

If another account has the username, the answer is a 409.

Log in with an account's username and password.

A username with no account and a wrong password get the same answer, a
401, so it doesn't tell which usernames have an account.

get.description:
Return the account the player is logged in with.

If the player isn't logged in, or their session expired, the answer is a
401. Once a day at most, the session is renewed: it then lasts 30 days
from now, and so does its cookie.

delete.description:
Log out: the session ends, and the browser forgets its cookie.

The answer is the same if the player wasn't logged in.

Ability.title: Ability
Ability.description: A unit ability (rules, section 7). A unit has at most one.

Account.title: Account
Account.description: The account of the player who is logged in: never its password's hash.

CardRedrawn.title: CardRedrawn
CardRedrawn.description:
The player swapped a card before round 1: ``engine.CardRedrawn``.

The player only gets this for their own cards. For the opponent's, they get
``OpponentRedrew``.

CardsDrawn.title: CardsDrawn
CardsDrawn.description:
The player drew cards: ``engine.CardsDrawn``.

The player only gets this for their own cards. For the opponent's, they get
``OpponentDrew``.

Choice.title: Choice
Choice.description: A card a player may put in a deck they build, and how many copies at most.

Choices.title: Choices
Choices.description:
What a player may put in a deck they build from a faction's cards.

``cards`` holds each card once, in the order the deck would hold them: the
faction's units, then the special cards. Every deck needs at least
``min_units`` units and may have at most ``max_specials`` special cards.
The rules decide all of it, so the API says it (ADR 0002).

Credentials.title: Credentials
Credentials.description:
What a player sends to make an account or to log in.

A username is 3 to 20 lower-case letters, digits, ``_`` or ``-``, so two
usernames that look the same are the same. A password is 8 to 128
characters, any of them: at least 8, as NIST asks (SP 800-63B), and at
most 128, so a hash never has to be worked out from a huge one.

DeckChoice.title: DeckChoice
DeckChoice.description:
What a player sends to build a deck or change one: all of it at once.

``deck`` is the id of the faction's own deck, whose cards it holds, and
``copies`` how many copies of each card the player chose, by the card's
id. A count is a whole number, never ``true`` (strict): JSON has no
integers of its own, and Python counts ``True`` as 1. There are far fewer
cards to choose than 64, the most ``copies`` may hold.

DeckStats.title: DeckStats
DeckStats.description: How the player's matches with one deck ended: how many of each.

DeckSummary.title: DeckSummary
DeckSummary.description: A deck the player can choose: its id, to start a match, and its name.

Decks.title: Decks
Decks.description:
The decks a player can choose from, in alphabetical order of their ids.

The answer is an object with a list in it, not a bare list, like every
other answer of the API, so it can get more fields later.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
What the API sends when it turns a request down.

``code`` says what went wrong, for the browser, and ``message`` says it in
words, for a person. A message may say where in the request the mistake
is, even with the name of a field the API doesn't know, but it never holds
a value from the request: a value can be nested too deep to send back.
A request over 16 KB never reaches the API: nginx turns it down with a
page of its own, not this error.

HornPlayed.title: HornPlayed
HornPlayed.description: A player played a War Horn: ``engine.HornPlayed``.

Match.title: Match
Match.description:
A match as the player may see it: its id, its version, the view and the rounds.

The id is all it takes to see and play the match, so only its player gets
it. The version goes up each time the match changes: a move sends back the
version of the view it was chosen from. ``rounds`` holds the end of each
round that ended, in order, so a page that comes back to a match knows how
those went.

MatchEnded.title: MatchEnded
MatchEnded.description: A player has no lives left: ``engine.MatchEnded``.

MatchSummary.title: MatchSummary
MatchSummary.description:
A match in the list of the player's matches.

``deck`` is the id of the player's deck and ``ai_deck`` that of the AI's.
When the player played a deck they built, ``deck`` is its faction's and
``deck_name`` the name it had then; otherwise ``deck_name`` is None.
``level`` is the level of the AI. ``result`` is None while the match goes
on: the player can get it by its id and play on.

Matches.title: Matches
Matches.description:
A page of the player's matches, the newest first.

``more`` says whether older ones are left: the next page comes from
asking for those before the last match of this one.

Move.title: Move
Move.description:
What the player sends to play: an action, and the version it was chosen at.

``action`` is one of the legal actions of the view, sent back as it is,
and ``version`` is the version of the match that came with that view. If
the match is at another version by then, the move isn't played.

MovePlayed.title: MovePlayed
MovePlayed.description:
One action played, as the player may see it: its events and the view after.

With the view after each action, the page can show the match as it was
then while it plays the action's events out, and not the match as it is
once every action is played.

NewMatch.title: NewMatch
NewMatch.description:
What the player sends to start a match: the deck they play, and the AI's level.

Either ``deck``, the id of a faction's own deck (``{"deck": "humans"}``),
or ``my_deck``, the id of a deck they built, while they are logged in:
one of the two, never both. ``level`` is how well the AI plays: ``easy``
is the baseline AI, ``normal`` and ``hard`` the Monte Carlo AI, which
guesses the cards it can't see (ADR 0018). Without it, ``easy``.

NothingToRevive.title: NothingToRevive
NothingToRevive.description: A Medic found no unit to revive: ``engine.NothingToRevive``.

OpponentDrew.title: OpponentDrew
OpponentDrew.description: The opponent drew cards, but not which: ``engine.OpponentDrew``.

OpponentRedrew.title: OpponentRedrew
OpponentRedrew.description: The opponent swapped a card, but not which: ``engine.OpponentRedrew``.

Pass.title: Pass
Pass.description: Take no more turns this round: ``engine.Pass``.

PlayScarecrow.title: PlayScarecrow
PlayScarecrow.description: Play a Scarecrow in place of a unit: ``engine.PlayScarecrow``.

PlaySpecial.title: PlaySpecial
PlaySpecial.description: Play a special card that needs no choice: ``engine.PlaySpecial``.

PlayUnit.title: PlayUnit
PlayUnit.description: Play a unit from the hand: ``engine.PlayUnit``.

Played.title: Played
Played.description:
A match after actions were played in it, and what happened.

``moves`` holds those actions, in order: in a new match, the AI's first
ones, if it starts (none if the player does); after the player's action,
that action and then the AI's answer, one move for each of its actions.
The ``view`` of the match is that of the last move, if there is one.

PlayerDeck.title: PlayerDeck
PlayerDeck.description: A deck a player built, with its id, as they chose it.

PlayerDecks.title: PlayerDecks
PlayerDecks.description:
The decks of the player who is logged in, the oldest first.

``most`` is how many decks a player may keep.

PlayerView.title: PlayerView
PlayerView.description: What one player may see of a match, as ``engine.PlayerView`` describes it.

Result.title: Result
Result.description:
How a match ended.

``outcome`` says whether the player won, lost or drew, ``rounds`` holds
each round's totals, in order, and ``ended_at`` when the last action was
played.

Revive.title: Revive
Revive.description: Revive a unit after a Medic: ``engine.Revive``.

RoundEnded.title: RoundEnded
RoundEnded.description: Both players passed and the round was scored: ``engine.RoundEnded``.

RoundScores.title: RoundScores
RoundScores.description: A round's totals when it ended: the player's and the AI's.

Row.title: Row
Row.description: A row of the board (rules, section 2).

RowView.title: RowView
RowView.description: One row on one side of the board, as ``engine.RowView`` describes it.

RowsView.title: RowsView
RowsView.description:
One side of the board: its three rows, by name.

The engine keeps them in a mapping from each ``Row``. Here each row has a
field of its own, so the JSON is the same, but the JSON schema says that
all three are always there.

ScarecrowPlayed.title: ScarecrowPlayed
ScarecrowPlayed.description: A player swapped a Scarecrow for a unit: ``engine.ScarecrowPlayed``.

SideView.title: SideView
SideView.description: What both players see of one player, as ``engine.SideView`` describes it.

SpecialCard.title: SpecialCard
SpecialCard.description:
A special card, as ``engine.SpecialCard`` describes it.

``weather_row`` is the row a weather card hits, on both sides of the board,
or null for any other special card. It is a rule, so the API says it: the
page doesn't know the rules (ADR 0002). So is ``description``: what the
card does.

SpecialKind.title: SpecialKind
SpecialKind.description: The effect of a special card (rules, section 8).

Stats.title: Stats
Stats.description:
How the player's matches ended with each deck they played.

Matches that go on don't count, and a deck with none that ended isn't
listed.

UnitCard.title: UnitCard
UnitCard.description:
A unit, as ``engine.UnitCard`` describes it.

``opponent_side`` says whether the unit goes on the side of the opponent
of who plays it or revives it, as a Spy does. It is a rule, so the API
says it: the page doesn't know the rules (ADR 0002). So is
``description``: what the card does, one sentence per thing.

UnitMustered.title: UnitMustered
UnitMustered.description: A Muster called a unit from the deck or hand: ``engine.UnitMustered``.

UnitPlayed.title: UnitPlayed
UnitPlayed.description: A player played a unit from their hand: ``engine.UnitPlayed``.

UnitRevived.title: UnitRevived
UnitRevived.description: A player revived a unit with a Medic: ``engine.UnitRevived``.

UnitView.title: UnitView
UnitView.description: A unit on the board, as ``engine.UnitView`` describes it.

WeatherPlayed.title: WeatherPlayed
WeatherPlayed.description: A player played a weather card: ``engine.WeatherPlayed``.
